item.title: Testing the Hypothesis That Culture Is Parasitic on Unsatisfied Human Needs
item.description: Finds good evidence that some cultural use compensates for frustrated needs and that some digital affects are self-reinforcing, but reserves the stronger label “parasitic” for systems shown to benefit from recurrent unresolved need rather than inferring dependence from market size or cultural popularity.

item.title: Intergenerational Extraction in Liberal Democracies
item.description: Finds a real democratic vulnerability to intergenerational burden shifting, but reserves the term extraction for cases where politically advantaged present cohorts improve their lifetime net position by externalizing uncompensated costs to younger or future cohorts.

item.title: Republicans as Moderating Opposition Without a Rival Order
item.description: A current-through-2026 test of the Republican moderating-opposition thesis that finds genuine retrenchment in some mature policy domains but durable Republican replacement or state-building in welfare, taxation, trade, and immigration enforcement.

item.title: Liberalism, Social Disembedding, and Managed Dependency
item.description: Examines how modern liberal-capitalist societies shift dependency from inherited persons and communities toward markets, public administration, credentials, professions, and digital infrastructures, and asks when those systems expand practical freedom versus creating opaque or weakly contestable dependency.

item.title: Puritan Moral Psychology and the Genealogy of American Progressivism
item.description: Finds real Puritan influence through transformed Protestant reform and later national reception, while rejecting a single uninterrupted genealogy that reduces the heterogeneous and transnational Progressive movement to secularized New England moral psychology.

item.title: Fallen Aristocrats: Status Loss, Elite Conversion, and Political Reaction
item.description: A source-audited comparison of how former hereditary and estate-based elites convert residual prestige, networks, education, and organizational capacity after institutional privilege collapses.

item.title: Judges in the Judicial Process of the United States
item.description: A structured guide to U.S. judges and judicial offices across federal and state systems, including tenure, appointment, elections, powers, and pay.

item.title: Dead Symbols and their Worship
item.description: An intentionally severe, aphoristic essay arguing that parts of mathematical culture confuse abstraction, difficulty, and proximity to unsolved problems with intellectual strength, while undervaluing synthesis, closure, pedagogy, and completed mastery.

item.title: Brickmaking: History, Materials, Processes, and Production Planning
item.description: Covers brickmaking from raw-material preparation through forming, drying, firing, testing, environmental control, production-scale planning, and current kiln-decarbonization work, while distinguishing stable process knowledge from time-sensitive standards and project economics.

item.title: Critical Review of Major Official Financial-Crisis Inquiry Reports
item.description: Compares the FCIC and major U.K. inquiry reports with primary evidence on investment-bank supervision, housing policy, AIG and Bear Stearns rescue design, and shadow banking, distinguishing legitimate framing critique from unsupported claims of institutional intent.

item.title: Global Population Dynamics: Peaks in Population Level and Growth Rates
item.description: Distinguishes the historical peak in the global population growth rate from the still-projected peak in world population size, using the current UN World Population Prospects 2024 revision and its 2026 interim update.

item.title: Meme Culture and the “Borderer-Right” Style Hypothesis
item.description: Finds that a low-deference, antagonistic “borderer” meme style is plausible as a measurable construct but cannot be equated with the political right in advance: far-right evidence is substantial in some contexts, while taboo, ridicule, out-group hostility, and irony also occur in left-wing and other meme communities.

item.title: Testing a “Borderer” Meme-Style Hypothesis: A Research Framework
item.description: Replaces a circular right-aggression/left-empathy classification with a testable design in which political ideology and meme style are measured independently and the proposed borderer construct must demonstrate reliability, coherence, and cross-context predictive validity to survive.

item.title: Proudhon’s Mutualism: Property, Reciprocity, and Mutual Credit
item.description: A source-audited study of Proudhon’s evolving mutualism, from the 1840 critique of absolute property through reciprocal exchange, the 1849 People’s Bank, mature federalism, the later rehabilitation of dispersed property as counter-power, and the divergent French and American mutualist legacies.
